objective: Resolve all six TASK-006 review findings with fail-closed Stop handling, lossless UTF-8 SessionStart emission, and mutation-sensitive encoding tests while preserving the established production serialization and file-encoding behavior.
requirements: Make .ai/hooks/stop_guard.py convert UnicodeDecodeError and expected filesystem read failures from implementation.md or context.jsonl into exit code 2 with an explanatory stderr diagnostic.
Make .ai/hooks/session_start.py report unreadable UTF-8 inputs on stderr, omit only the unreadable input, continue injecting any remaining readable context, and exit 0.
Emit SessionStart context as explicit UTF-8 bytes so Japanese and other non-cp1252 text reaches stdout without UnicodeEncodeError when the Windows text layer uses cp1252.

Restore and strengthen Utf8RoundTripTests.test_context_block_round_trips_unicode and Utf8RoundTripTests.test_context_file_bytes_are_utf8 in place; use real non-ASCII JSON payload bytes in the test harness by temporarily forcing ensure_ascii=False without changing production json.dumps behavior.

Strengthen Utf8RoundTripTests.test_ascii_content_is_byte_for_byte_unchanged in place by comparing the produced artifact with independently constructed expected ASCII bytes rather than a decode-and-reencode identity.

Extend the existing AuditDiscriminatesTests class with explicitly named mutation regressions: test_removing_context_write_encoding_fails_the_round_trip_test, test_removing_context_read_encoding_fails_the_round_trip_test, test_removing_context_write_encoding_fails_the_bytes_test, and test_removing_context_write_encoding_fails_the_ascii_compatibility_test.

Implement mutation regressions by loading a temporary in-memory copy of orchestrator.py with the uniquely targeted encoding keyword removed and installing a scoped Path.open shim whose omitted-encoding default is deterministic UTF-16; for the Unicode context tests also force ensure_ascii=False in the test harness so removal is observable on every host.
Require every mutation regression to demonstrate a pass-to-fail transition: the corresponding restored test passes against the unmodified module and fails against the specifically mutated module.
Correct binary-mode detection for open(path, 'rb'), os.fdopen(fd, 'rb'), Path.open('rb'), and keyword mode forms while retaining detection of text calls lacking encoding.
Parse each scoped source once per unchanged source value while retaining an uncached source-text audit path for mutation tests.

Add Python39CompatibilityTests.test_touched_sources_parse_with_python39_grammar to parse all modified and created Python files with the Python 3.9 grammar supported by ast.parse(feature_version=(3, 9)).

Preserve valid hook behavior, including allowing a completed write-back, blocking an incomplete write-back, remaining quiet outside an orchestrated task, and continuing SessionStart injection when one optional input is unreadable.

files_to_modify.purpose: Centralize verdict-dependent UTF-8 reads and translate expected decode or read failures into an explanatory fail-closed exit code 2.
Add visible read-failure degradation and explicit UTF-8 stdout emission without changing the hook's non-blocking contract.

Restore and strengthen the three ineffective tests, add specifically named deterministic mutation proofs and Python 3.9 grammar coverage, correct binary-mode classification, and reuse parsed AST results.

files_to_create.purpose: Provide isolated subprocess regressions for malformed hook inputs, exit-code contracts, partial SessionStart degradation, and UTF-8 output through a cp1252-configured text layer; this file is currently untracked working-copy starting state and remains a created file for enforced diff scope.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Malformed UTF-8 in either Stop guard input blocks with exit code 2 and an explanatory stderr reason, while valid and incomplete write-back behavior retains its existing allow/block contract.
SessionStart exits 0 and preserves Japanese text as UTF-8 when its stdout text layer is forced to cp1252, while unreadable inputs are reported and readable remaining context is still emitted.

The original F4 and F5 test identities are restored and each encoding-sensitive assertion has a named deterministic mutation proof that fails when its uniquely targeted context encoding argument is removed.

The AST audit treats positional and keyword binary modes for built-in open, os.fdopen, and Path.open as binary, continues to report text calls without encoding, and reuses parsing only for unchanged source.

All touched Python files parse under Python 3.9 grammar, and the complete repository unittest suite is non-empty and passes under the validation interpreter; full runtime execution on Python 3.9 and 3.12 remains a required CI completion gate.
acceptance_criteria.verify: {python} -m unittest -v test_utf8_io.Python39CompatibilityTests.test_touched_sources_parse_with_python39_grammar && {python} -c "import unittest; s=unittest.defaultTestLoader.discover('.'); n=s.countTestCases(); print('discovered %d tests' % n); r=unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2).run(s); raise SystemExit(0 if n > 0 and r.wasSuccessful() else 1)"

constraints: Use only the Python standard library.
A Stop guard failure to read verdict-dependent input must fail closed with exit code 2 and a reason; it must never escape as exit code 1.
SessionStart remains a non-blocking injector: expected input read failures must be visible on stderr but must not return exit code 2.
Do not weaken, delete, rename, or repurpose the existing F4 and F5 test identities; strengthen their assertions in place.
Do not change production json.dumps behavior; ensure_ascii=False is confined to the test harness used to expose encoding behavior.

Keep the explicit UTF-8 file encoding arguments introduced by TASK-006 in .ai/scripts/orchestrator.py, .ai/scripts/review-package.py, .ai/hooks/session_start.py, and .ai/hooks/stop_guard.py exactly as established.
Do not change newline translation, _support.py text I/O, diff-scope base selection, unrelated attribute-call classification, or behavior beyond the six findings.
Maintain compatibility with Python 3.9 and Python 3.12; .github/workflows/ci.yml owns full multi-version execution and must not be modified.
Acceptance commands may invoke only the orchestrator-provided {python} interpreter and must reject an empty suite.

The pre-existing untracked test_hook_resilience.py and already modified test_utf8_io.py are starting-state work to be corrected; focused acceptance results are meaningful only together with AC-3's mutation proofs and AC-5's non-empty full-suite run.
Workflow hook changes are explicitly declared as required by the constitution and ADR-0004.
Do not modify task evidence, state.json, review artifacts, schemas, CI configuration, or other orchestrator-owned verdict artifacts.

Before approval, the orchestrator must update TASK-007 state so plan_file names plan-v3.json and present the SHA-256 of those exact bytes; this is orchestration state management, not an implementation file authorized by this contract.
risks: The previous plan's production architecture was structurally sound; rejection resulted from an unsatisfiable validation selector and inadequate mutation proof, so implementation should retain the existing hook design while correcting the contract and tests.

The working copy already contains partial TASK-007 hook and test changes; a green focused test can reflect pre-existing work rather than the completed task, which is why mutation-specific selectors and the guarded full-suite criterion are both required.

Writing to sys.stdout.buffer bypasses locale encoding as required, but test harnesses may replace stdout with a text-only object; fallback behavior must preserve content or report failure rather than silently discard injection.
Catching exceptions too broadly could hide programming defects, so hook handling should be limited to expected UnicodeDecodeError and filesystem read failures.

A SessionStart implementation that returns immediately after one unreadable input could still lose readable constitution or blackboard content; tests must cover partial degradation in both directions.

Mutation tests can produce false confidence if they remove an unrelated encoding keyword; each mutation must uniquely identify its production call and prove an unmodified-pass to mutated-fail transition.

The hostile-default Path.open shim must be scoped and restored reliably so it cannot contaminate other tests; UTF-16 is intentional because it makes omitted encoding observable even for an ASCII-only compatibility artifact.

ast.parse with a Python 3.9 feature version checks syntax compatibility but cannot prove runtime API compatibility; actual full-suite execution on both supported interpreters must remain a CI completion gate.
Path-only AST caching can return stale results after controlled mutation; mutation audits must use the uncached source-level helper.

The branch base remains over-inclusive relative to main, so diff-scope validation can report unrelated files until the orchestrator resolves its acknowledged base-state issue; this contract does not authorize changing that architecture.
Approval remains unsafe while state.json.plan_file points to plan-v2.json; the orchestrator must bind approval to plan-v3.json without adding state.json to implementation scope.
test_strategy: Run stop_guard.py from temporary repository-shaped directories with malformed implementation.md and context.jsonl bytes, asserting exit 2, useful stderr, no exit 1, and unchanged valid/incomplete write-back behavior.
Run session_start.py as a subprocess with Japanese context and a deliberately cp1252-configured stdout text layer, capture raw stdout bytes, and assert exact UTF-8 content and exit 0.
Test unreadable constitution and blackboard inputs independently, asserting a diagnostic and continued emission of whichever source remains readable.

Restore the original F4 test method names and temporarily force ensure_ascii=False only in their fixtures so context serialization writes genuine non-ASCII bytes while production serialization remains unchanged.
Build an independent expected byte sequence for the ASCII compatibility test and compare it directly with the produced artifact.

For each named mutation regression, first run the covered test against the normal module, then load source with exactly one required encoding keyword removed under a scoped UTF-16 default Path.open shim and assert that the same covered test fails.
Exercise AST helpers directly with built-in open, os.fdopen, Path.open, keyword binary mode, text-mode counterexamples, os.open exclusion, cache reuse, and uncached mutated source.

Parse every touched Python source with Python 3.9 grammar, then run the guarded non-empty full suite under the current validation interpreter; require the unchanged CI matrix to run the full suite on Python 3.9 and 3.12 before completion.
Treat AC-1, AC-2, and AC-4 as focused diagnostics, not standalone evidence: completion requires their conjunction with AC-3's mutation proof and AC-5's non-empty full-suite result.
